title: Chapter 3254 Tendrils of War
content:
"You did what?"

When the Jade Queen eventually joined them, her childish facade showed a crack for the first time.

Well, of course it did. Who would be able to maintain their composure after hearing that someone they knew declared a war on War?

Sitting in an ornate chair and staring at Cassie with a chilling smile, the Jade Queen remained silent for a short while. Then, in a deceptively relaxed tone, she said:

"I just want to make sure that I heard it properly. You said you declared war... on who?"

But Cassie seemed impervious to the dangerous undertone in the ancient monster's voice. She just shrugged calmly.

“The Empire. Why are you surprised?"

The Jade Queen studied her silently, then glanced at the rest of them and scoffed.

"Indeed, why am I surprised?"

Her gaze eventually landed on Sable.

"You there, young lady. Please explain to that person why I am surprised."

Sable coughed awkwardly.

"Uh... well... the esteemed queen is surprised because one does not usually declare war on gods. Unless they are tired of living. Even then, there are easier ways to die."

The Jade Queen nodded with a smile.

"See! Sable gets it!"

Cassie simply shook her head.

"Stop pretending.”

She turned slightly, facing the Jade Queen, and continued in a measured tone:

“You must have been aware for a long time that the Empire would not leave you alone. That is because the Empire won't leave anyone alone. It will continue to expand, and expand, and expand — until it swallows all mortal realms and makes all creatures populating them either submit to the Dragon... or die. So, now is our last chance to make a stand."

Cassie smiled darkly.

“Or were you planning to abandon your beautiful palace, surrender your lands, and run away to one of the Divine Realms? If not, then you knew all along that, one day, you would have to fight the Empire once more. All I did was move up the date."

Her smile turned a little mischievous.

“Surely, you aren't angry about a little thing like that?"

The Jade Queen stared at her silently for a while, then scoffed.

There was a hint of disbelief in her usually confident voice.

“Will you listen to that madwoman talk... the gall, the audacity!"

Then, she stared at Cassie intensely.

"Well, fine. I'll admit it. I did know that the tendrils of the Empire would reach my lands one day in the future... maybe even one day soon. But, what? A war? Goodness gracious, how uncouth. Who says I was going to go to war with the Dragon?"

She laughed.

“What's wrong with being under the Empire? As long as you are strong enough, even the Dragon won't treat you badly. The Supreme rulers of the imperial provinces live quite lavishly, you know. All you have to do is put up a gaudy statue of War God in some dark corner and bow to it from time to time. What's the big deal?"

The Jade Queen raised her chin proudly.

“Besides, I am quite an accomplished genius in the art of war. Won't the Empire welcome me with open arms? I killed two of their Spirits, after all. That means that there are three empty spots left in their pantheon. Someone of my stunning beauty would fit quite nicely on a temple dais, don't you think? Ah, I can just imagine. A statue of me displayed in every mortal realm..."

She struck a subtle pose and smiled, looking down her nose at them with something that resembled an attempt at gracious benevolence.

Nephis spared her a cold gaze.

“Were you really considering surrendering to the Empire?"

The Jade Queen held her gaze for a few moments, then sighed and slumped in her chair.

“Of course not. Me, serving another monarch? Preposterous! Everyone can serve the Jade Queen, but the Jade Queen serves no one."

She remained silent for a moment, glancing into the distance, and then added in a somber tone:

“Empire... is like the great volcano whose shadow looms over my palace. It seethes and smolders, filling the hearts of mortals who populate this land with dread. But what can they do? Even if they know that the volcano will erupt one day, they are powerless to stop it. All they can do is look at the rising smoke and tremble in fear."

Turning back to face them, she smiled coldly.

“Of course, I am not powerless against the volcano, and neither do I know how to tremble in fear. But War God? He is an unstoppable calamity even for demigods like us."

At that moment, Mordret spoke, his tone infused with a subtle sense of surprise.

“But you are the only person who has ever managed to defeat the Empire. You even killed two of its Sacred rulers. That is why joining forces with you is so vital for us... surely, if you repelled the imperial legions once, you can do it again — with powerful allies such as ourselves standing by your side, no less."

The Jade Queen studied him for a long while, then slowly shook her head.

"No. Do not think that I am capable of defeating the Empire for the second time."

She sighed.

“That is because the Imperial Spirits are no fools. They make mistakes, but they never make the same mistake twice... back then, they were undefeated, unstoppable, arrogant. That was why I could turn the tide of war against them."

The Jade Queen leaned back in her ornate chair and smiled ominously.

"You should understand how the Empire operated back then. The Spirits rarely moved personally as long as there were no opponents of equal Rank for them to defeat. For minor realms, the Empire would send conquering legions — mundane and Awakened soldiers, Ascended officers, and Transcendent generals. It was only in case the legions were defeated that one of the High Priests, a Supreme being, would enter the battlefield personally."

Her golden eyes glinted.

“And if a High Priest fell... then, finally, one of the Spirits would descend upon the battlefield.”

She shook her head.

"My case was quite unique, though. The Empire showed me some face, sending two of them at the same time. Well... maybe not. Those two had always been a pair, following each other around — the twins. However, they couldn't stand each other. So, that was what I used."

Her smile turned a little wicked.

"Fools are easy to manipulate... the arrogant sages who think themselves invincible are easier by far."

The Jade Queen chuckled.

“There was already a wedge between them, and I drove it deeper. I turned them against each other and killed one with the hands of the other. Then, I caught the victor by surprise and delivered a fatal blow before he could recover... even though he had already been weakened, it took him a while to die. Still, all I had to do was endure until the poison took hold."

The smile slowly drained from her face.

“But we won't be able to use the same trick again. The remaining Imperial Spirits are far more astute — they had always been, and after losing two of their own and tasting the humiliation of defeat, they won't underestimate the enemy again. Victory, Beauty, Art, and Joy... do not take them lightly. They had not inherited the throne of the Dragon by chance."

She hesitated for a moment, then sighed.

“But, truly, it is not fighting the Spirits that we should be wary of. The true peril hides in what will happen if we do manage to slay one... or a few."

Nephis raised an eyebrow.

“And what, exactly, will happen?"

The Jade Queen looked at her in surprise.

“Why... once a High Priest dies, a Spirit comes. Who comes when a Spirit dies, then?"

She smiled darkly.

“The Dragon."

The Jade Queen looked away with a somber expression.

“Even if I defeated the Spirit of Conquest and the Spirit of Valor, I had not defeated the Empire of War. Because as soon as they fell, War itself came knocking. He fell from the sky like a comet, his roar paralyzing every fiber of my being with utter terror."

She shivered and fell silent. A few moments later, though, she added in a subdued tone:

“That was centuries ago. Back then, the Dragon was already distancing himself from the minutiae of running the Empire and rarely showed himself, but he had not become as reclusive as he is today yet. Still, it only took him a few moments to descend when two of his Sacred apostles were killed.”

Sunny frowned.

"And yet, here you are. The Empire was defeated, and the Jade Palace still stands. So how did you survive an encounter with War God?"

The Jade Queen stared at him for a long while, her expression slowly turning grim. Then, she suddenly giggled.

“What, do you think those War Spirits are the only ones who can cry and call daddy when they get into trouble? I have a divine patron, too!"

The Jade Queen grinned.

“A heartbeat after the Dragon appeared, the Demon of Dread was there as well. And he wasn't happy to see me getting bullied, either. Oh, my! For a few moments there, I was afraid that the adults would get into a fight too."

The Jade Queen smiled wistfully, then sighed.

“But in the end, they talked it over and parted peacefully. I guess War decided to show my daemon some courtesy. That was how I managed to defeat the Empire, kill two of its Spirits, and stay alive despite doing all that."

She hesitated for a short while, then added in a more somber tone:

"Don't expect that it will happen again, though. The Demon of Dread will not come to our defense if we anger War God... he has been gone for hundreds of years, building something in some distant hell."

A bitter note found its way into her voice.

“Sometimes, I think he forgot that I exist altogether. But then again, all of them have grown distant and elusive — the daemons, the gods... it is the Age of Humans, after all. The Golden Age"

In the silence that followed, her heavy sigh sounded especially loud.

The Jade Queen remained silent for a long while, then turned to look intently at Cassie.

A malevolent smile split her tantalizing face, and her golden eyes flashed with a sinister glow.

“Fine... let's spill some blood on that gold, then. Everyone knows that the Jade Queen is the only one who has defeated the Empire; shall we make me the only one who has defeated the Empire twice?"
